newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan leader takes pistol to work - source.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan leader takes pistol to work - source.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera, 81, can hit the bullseye on a rifle range and takes a pistol to work every day, a source close to Latin America's oldest leader said on Thursday, playing down rumours that he is ill.
The government has flatly rejected reports last month that Caldera has Parkinson's disease, a brain disorder that causes muscle weakness, and says he is fit.
Caldera carries a .38 calibre Smith & Wesson pistol and places it on his desk every morning before starting work, the source said.

"It's an old pistol, maybe 50 years old, but it's well maintained," he told Reuters. "He loves to shoot and practices whenever he can...it's a habit he never lost from the old days of Venezuelan politics."

After the reports of his illness surfaced, Caldera projected a robust image, walking the 500 yards (meters) between Miraflores presidential palace and Congress after delivering his annual televised message to the nation.
